Upper bounds for the query and gate complexities are derived in the limit of large grid sizes and found to be polynomially larger than the time complexity of the corresponding classical algorithms, primarily due to the dimension, sparsity, and norm of the Carleman-linearized evolution matrix. The convergence criteria are shown to impose severe restrictions on physically relevant plasma applications, requiring dissipation levels far exceeding those provided by the Krook operator.

.
tldr: The paper investigates a Carleman-linearization-based quantum algorithm for solving the nonlinear electrostatic Vlasov equation with Krook collisions, finding polynomial complexity overhead and severe convergence restrictions.
motivation: To assess whether quantum computers can practically solve nonlinear ODEs arising in plasma physics, specifically the Vlasov equation, by comparing quantum algorithm complexity to classical methods.
method: The Vlasov equation is discretized on a (1+1)-dimensional phase-space grid and mapped to the input of a Carleman-linearization quantum algorithm, with upper bounds derived for query and gate complexities in the large-grid limit.
result: Query and gate complexities are polynomially larger than the time complexity of classical algorithms, mainly due to the dimension, sparsity, and norm of the Carleman-linearized evolution matrix; convergence criteria require dissipation levels far beyond those provided by the Krook operator.
conclusion: The quantum algorithm does not offer practical advantage for this plasma application, as the required dissipation severely restricts physical relevance and the complexity scaling is unfavorable.

title: On The Relation Between Perspective-neutral, Algebraic, And Effective Quantum Reference Frames
authors: Julian de Vuyst, Philipp A. Hoehn, And Artur Tsobanjan
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2196 (2026).

The framework of internal quantum reference frames (QRFs) constitutes a universal toolset for dealing with symmetries in quantum theory and has led to new revelations in quantum gravity, gauge theories and foundational physics. Multiple approaches have emerged, sometimes differing in scope and the way symmetries are implemented, raising the question as to their relation. Here, we investigate the relation between three approaches to QRFs for gauge symmetries, namely the [MATH] semiclassical, [MATH], and [MATH] (PN) approaches. Rather than constructing Hilbert spaces, as the PN approach, the effective approach is based on a quantum phase space parametrized by expectation values and fluctuations, while the emphasis of the algebraic approach is on the state space of complex linear functionals on a kinematical algebra. Nevertheless, external frame information is treated as gauge in all three formalisms, manifested in constraints on states and algebra. We show that these three approaches are, in fact, equivalent for ideal QRFs, distinguished by sharp orientations, which is the previous setting of the first two approaches. Our demonstration pertains to single constraints, including relativistic ones, and encompasses QRF changes. In particular, the QRF transformations of the PN framework agree semiclassically with those of the older effective approach, by which it was inspired. As a physical application, we explore the QRF covariance of uncertainties and fluctuations, which turn out to be frame dependent. This is particularly well-suited for the effective and algebraic approaches, for which these quantities form a natural basis. Finally, we pave the way towards extending these two approaches to non-ideal QRFs by studying the projection and gauge-fixing operations of the Page-Wootters formalism, built into the PN framework, on algebraic states.

.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between perspective-neutral, algebraic, and effective approaches to ideal quantum reference frames for gauge symmetries, with applications to frame-dependent uncertainties.
motivation: Multiple quantum reference frame frameworks have emerged with differing scopes and symmetry implementations, creating a need to clarify their relations and unify the formalism.
method: The authors compare the three approaches by analyzing their state spaces, constraints, and QRF transformations, proving equivalence for ideal QRFs with sharp orientations and single constraints, including relativistic cases, and studying Page-Wootters projection and gauge-fixing on algebraic states.
result: The three approaches are equivalent for ideal QRFs, the perspective-neutral QRF transformations agree semiclassically with the effective approach, and uncertainties/fluctuations are shown to be frame dependent.
conclusion: This work provides a unified understanding of quantum reference frame formalisms and paves the way for extending the effective and algebraic approaches to non-ideal QRFs.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Nuclear Dynamics In First Quantization
authors: Luca Spagnoli, Chiara Lissoni, And Alessandro Roggero
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2200 (2026).

The study of real time dynamics of nuclear systems is of great importance to provide theoretical predictions of cross sections relevant for both terrestrial experiments as well as applications in astrophysics. First principles simulations of these dynamical processes is however hindered by an exponential cost in classical resources and the possibility of performing scalable simulations using quantum computers is currently an active field of research. In this work we provide the first complete characterization of the resource requirements for studying nuclear dynamics with the full Leading Order (LO) pionless EFT Hamiltonian in first quantization employing simulation strategies using both product formulas as well as Quantum Signal Processing. In particular, we show that time evolution of such an Hamiltonian can be performed with polynomial resources in the number of particles, and logarithmic resources in the number of single-particle basis states. This result provides an exponential improvement compared with previous work on the same Hamiltonian model in second quantization. We find that interesting simulations for low energy nuclear scattering could be achievable with tens of millions of T gates and few hundred logical qubits suggesting that the study of simple nuclear reactions could be amenable for early fault tolerant quantum platforms.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the resource requirements for quantum simulation of real-time nuclear dynamics using the LO pionless EFT Hamiltonian in first quantization with product formulas and quantum signal processing.
motivation: First-principles simulations of nuclear dynamics are exponentially costly on classical computers, motivating the use of quantum computers for scalable predictions of scattering cross sections.
method: The authors analyze and compare product formulas and quantum signal processing for time evolution under the LO pionless EFT Hamiltonian in first quantization, focusing on T-gate and logical qubit counts.
result: They show polynomial scaling in particle number and logarithmic scaling in single-particle basis size, an exponential improvement over previous second-quantized approaches, with feasible simulations requiring tens of millions of T gates and few hundred logical qubits.
conclusion: Simple low-energy nuclear scattering simulations may be achievable on early fault-tolerant quantum platforms, though the work is a quantum simulation resource analysis rather than a contribution to the defined quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems directions.

title: Hybrid Vqe-cvqe Algorithm Using Diabatic State Preparation
authors: C Stephen Hellberg And Daniel Gunlycke John P T Stenger
abstract: We propose a hybrid variational quantum algorithm that has variational parameters used by both the quantum circuit and the subsequent classical optimization. Similar to the variational quantum eigensolver, this algorithm applies a parameterized unitary operator to the qubit register. We generate this operator using diabatic state preparation. The quantum measurement results then inform the classical optimization procedure used by the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver. We demonstrate the algorithm on a system of interacting electrons and show how it can be used on long-term error-corrected as well as short-term intermediate-scale quantum computers. Our simulations performed on IBM Brisbane produced energies well within chemical accuracy.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid variational quantum algorithm that combines diabatic state preparation with a cascaded classical optimizer to improve VQE for electronic structure problems.
motivation: Variational quantum eigensolvers are promising for near-term quantum computers, but their performance depends critically on efficient state preparation and optimization strategies.
method: The authors use diabatic state preparation to generate a parameterized unitary operator applied to a qubit register, then feed measurement outcomes into a classical optimization routine (cascaded VQE).
result: Simulations on IBM Brisbane for interacting electrons produced ground-state energies within chemical accuracy, and the scheme is argued to be suitable for both error-corrected and NISQ devices.
conclusion: The hybrid VQE-CVQE approach offers a practical route to accurate quantum chemistry simulations, though its broader relevance to quantum information theory remains limited.

title: Anderson Localization As Modal Phase Decoherence In Disordered Monoatomic Phononic Chains
authors: S Adhikari
abstract: Anderson localization in one-dimensional disordered media is traditionally characterized through transfer-matrix growth and Lyapunov exponents in the infinite-chain limit. Although mathematically rigorous, this approach obscures the underlying physical mechanism and requires extrapolation for finite systems. We develop an alternative formulation rooted in the modal decomposition of finite disordered chains and random eigenvalues. Starting from time-domain impulse response analysis, we show that disorder-induced eigenvalue scatter causes each modal contribution to acquire a random phase deviation that grows linearly in time, producing a Gaussian decay of the ensemble-averaged modal amplitude with a characteristic decoherence time inversely proportional to both the disorder strength and the eigenvalue variance. This modal phase decoherence manifests in the frequency domain as exponential decay of transmission amplitude, which we express exactly for any finite chain length via a spectral product over eigenvalue detunings derived from Cramer’s rule. For Gaussian disorder, the ensemble-averaged localization factor is obtained in closed form using Dawson’s integral; for uniform disorder an exact elementary expression is derived. We prove rigorously that the localization factor is independent of the disorder distribution to leading order, depending only on the variance, establishing Anderson localization as a second-moment statistical process. The continuum limit recovers the classical transfer-matrix prediction for the coupling-parameter dependence, and Monte Carlo simulations confirm that the disorder-to-coupling ratio is the fundamental dimensionless parameter governing weak-to-strong localization transitions, with the scaled localization factor collapsing onto a universal master curve. The formulation provides exact finite-system results without infinite-chain extrapolation and offers direct physical insight into the decoherence mechanism underlying Anderson localization.
tldr: The paper develops a modal phase decoherence formulation of Anderson localization in finite one-dimensional disordered phononic chains, deriving exact finite-system expressions for the localization factor and universal scaling.
motivation: Traditional transfer-matrix and Lyapunov exponent approaches obscure the physical mechanism of Anderson localization and require infinite-chain extrapolation.
method: The authors analyze time-domain impulse responses of finite disordered chains, showing disorder-induced eigenvalue scatter causes random modal phase deviations that grow linearly in time and lead to Gaussian decay of ensemble-averaged modal amplitudes.
result: They obtain exact closed-form localization factors for Gaussian and uniform disorder, prove distribution-independence to leading order, and find a universal master curve governed by the disorder-to-coupling ratio.
conclusion: The work provides a physical decoherence-based interpretation of Anderson localization and exact finite-system results without infinite-chain extrapolation, though it lies outside the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Intrinsic Phase-locking Of Terahertz Auto-oscillations In The Easy-plane Antiferromagnet Mn2Au
authors: Yiyue Wang, Wenbo Zhang, Hao-Hsuan Chen, Milad Jalali, Andrea Meo And Yaowen Liu
abstract: Antiferromagnets offer a promising platform for ultrafast spintronic emitters owing to their intrinsic terahertz ( ) spin dynamics, yet the mechanisms governing the onset and coherence of current-driven oscillations remain poorly understood. Here we develop a multiscale theoretical framework for the collinear antiferromagnet Mn2Au driven by a perpendicularly polarized spin current. Using a momentum-dependent canonical transformation of the coupled macrospin Hamiltonian, we show that the emergence of auto-oscillations is governed by a saddle-node bifurcation set by the in-plane fourfold anisotropy barrier. Moreover, we identify an intrinsic phase-locking mechanism that is threshold-free: once auto-oscillations are initiated, the interplay between easy-plane anisotropy and strong antiferromagnetic (AFM) exchange generates a robust restoring force that stabilizes the relative phase of the two sublattices throughout the simulated limit cycle. This behavior contrasts sharply with that of antiferromagnets with perpendicular anisotropy, where phase unlocking can destabilize the dynamics. Zero-temperature atomistic spin-dynamics (ASDs) simulations support the collective phase-locking picture in the full lattice model, and three independent K atomistic ASD spot checks show bounded thermal fluctuations, no phase slips, and a persistent spectral peak near THz. Stochastic two-sublattice collective-mode tests over – further indicate milliradian-scale relative-phase noise and show that a Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction-like perturbation mainly produces a static relative-phase offset rather than unlocking. Our results support Mn2Au as a highly coherent platform for continuous-wave generation and provide general design principles for stable AFM oscillators. Here, threshold-free refers to the absence of an additional microscopic relative-phase-locking threshold; the macroscopic onset of auto-oscillation remains finite and is set by the in-plane fourfold anisotropy barrier.
tldr: A multiscale theoretical study of current-driven terahertz auto-oscillations in the collinear antiferromagnet Mn2Au, identifying an intrinsic threshold-free phase-locking mechanism set by easy-plane anisotropy and strong AFM exchange.
motivation: Antiferromagnets are promising for ultrafast spintronic THz emitters, but the mechanisms governing the onset and coherence of current-driven oscillations are poorly understood.
method: The authors develop a multiscale framework using a momentum-dependent canonical transformation of the coupled macrospin Hamiltonian, supported by zero-temperature atomistic spin-dynamics simulations and stochastic two-sublattice collective-mode tests.
result: Auto-oscillation onset is governed by a saddle-node bifurcation set by the in-plane fourfold anisotropy barrier, and a robust intrinsic phase-locking mechanism stabilizes the relative sublattice phase with milliradian-scale noise and no phase slips.
conclusion: Mn2Au is proposed as a highly coherent platform for continuous-wave THz generation, with general design principles for stable AFM oscillators.

title: Transverse Geometry Reshapes Current And Tracer Fluctuation Amplitudes In Quasi-one-dimensional Single Files
authors: Olivier Bénichou And Aurélien Grabsch
abstract: Single-file transport means no overtaking: particles move in a narrow channel while preserving their longitudinal order. This simple constraint has profound dynamical consequences, most notably tracer subdiffusion, and has made single-file transport a paradigmatic form of confined many-body motion, observed from molecular transport in zeolites to single-file diffusion of colloids in narrow channels. A common modelling approach assumes that, once overtaking is suppressed, finite-width effects can be discarded or represented by an effective particle size in a strictly one-dimensional model. Starting from the Brownian dynamics in the full confined geometry, we instead derive the exact large-scale one-dimensional fluctuating-hydrodynamic equation governing the coarse-grained line density. Its transport coefficients are fixed by the confined equilibrium equation of state, through which the transverse geometry remains encoded in the one-dimensional description. Consequently, transverse geometry leaves the single-file scaling unchanged but can qualitatively reshape the density dependence of the current and tracer fluctuation amplitudes. In the minimal hard-core setting, this yields a collective diffusivity that can become non-monotonic in density for sufficiently wide no-passing channels. This geometric non-monotonicity propagates to exact large-scale predictions for the amplitudes of integrated-current fluctuations and tracer-displacement fluctuations. The effect is robust to the interaction potential, channel geometry, initial preparation and microscopic dynamics. Quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport therefore defines a distinct regime in which forbidding overtaking does not erase geometry from collective transport.
tldr: Exact fluctuating hydrodynamics shows that transverse confinement geometry reshapes current and tracer fluctuation amplitudes in quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport without changing the subdiffusive scaling.
motivation: Single-file transport is often modeled as strictly one-dimensional, discarding finite-width effects or replacing them by an effective particle size; the authors ask instead how the full transverse geometry influences large-scale collective behavior.
method: Starting from Brownian dynamics in a confined geometry, they derive the exact large-scale one-dimensional fluctuating hydrodynamic equation whose transport coefficients are fixed by the confined equilibrium equation of state.
result: Transverse geometry leaves the single-file scaling unchanged but can qualitatively reshape the density dependence of current and tracer fluctuation amplitudes; in the hard-core case, the collective diffusivity can become non-monotonic in density for sufficiently wide no-passing channels.
conclusion: Quasi-one-dimensional single-file transport defines a distinct regime in which forbidding overtaking does not erase geometry from collective transport.

title: Coherent Electron Transmission Across Twin Boundaries In Cu(111)
authors: Jungin Yeo, Gahee Lee, Su Jae Kim, Seong-Gon Kim, Heeyeon Lee, Minseong Kwon, Young Duck Kim, Se-Young Jeong And Sangjun Jeon
abstract: Copper thin films are foundational to modern electronics and nanotechnology, yet their charge transport is limited fundamentally by electron scattering at atomic-scale imperfections. Recent advances in atomic sputtering epitaxy (ASE) have enabled the growth of grain-boundary–free Cu(111) films, but defects such as twin boundaries and atomic step edges persist as intrinsic scattering centers. Here, we report that scanning tunneling spectroscopy measurements on Cu(111) films reveal pronounced quantum interference, indicating non-dephasing, elastic scattering across these atomically sharp discontinuities. The structural symmetry of the discontinuities, combined with identical Fermi surface on either side of the interface, facilitates unexpectedly high transmission probabilities and preserve phase coherence—fundamentally distinguishing ASE grown single crystalline thin films from the diffusive transport characteristic found in polycrystalline copper. These findings reveal that despite the presence of atomic discontinuities, Cu(111) can support highly transparent, coherent electron flow without invoking topological protection. These findings establish a framework of utilizing conventional metals in coherent, low-dissipation nanoscale electronic devices.
tldr: Coherent electron transmission across twin boundaries in Cu(111) films is observed via scanning tunneling spectroscopy, showing high transmission and phase coherence due to structural symmetry and identical Fermi surfaces.
motivation: Copper thin films are limited by electron scattering at atomic-scale defects like twin boundaries; understanding whether these defects preserve coherence could enable low-dissipation nanoscale electronics.
method: Scanning tunneling spectroscopy measurements on grain-boundary-free Cu(111) films grown by atomic sputtering epitaxy to probe quantum interference and transmission across twin boundaries and atomic step edges.
result: Pronounced quantum interference indicates non-dephasing elastic scattering across twin boundaries, with unexpectedly high transmission probabilities and preserved phase coherence due to the structural symmetry and identical Fermi surface on either side.
conclusion: Cu(111) can support highly transparent, coherent electron flow despite atomic discontinuities, without invoking topological protection, establishing a framework for using conventional metals in coherent, low-dissipation nanoscale electronic devices.

title: Quantum Control And The Topological Properties Of The Magnon Photo-transport In Two-dimensional Collinear Ferromagnet
authors: Jun-Cen Li And An Du
abstract: In this work, we investigate light-induced magnon spin photocurrent (MSPC) and magnon energy photocurrent (MEPC) via the Aharonov–Casher (AC) effect. We treat the influence of the electric field through the AC effect as a perturbative term. Subsequently, we derived explicit expressions for MSPC and MEPC in a two-dimensional, collinear ferromagnetic system. Our theoretical framework is applied to both Hexagonal and Kagome two-dimensional ferromagnetic lattices. We demonstrate that MSPC and MEPC can be modulated by tuning the optical frequency and the material’s relaxation time. Furthermore, in the low-frequency and infinite-relaxation-time limit, longitudinal MS(E)PC correlates with the topological properties of the magnon system.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates light-induced magnon spin and energy photocurrents via the Aharonov-Casher effect in two-dimensional collinear ferromagnets, linking transport to topological properties.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how quantum control and topological features influence magnon photocurrents in 2D ferromagnetic materials.
method: They treat the electric field through the Aharonov-Casher effect as a perturbation and derive explicit expressions for magnon spin and energy photocurrents, applying the framework to hexagonal and kagome lattices.
result: The magnon spin and energy photocurrents can be tuned by optical frequency and relaxation time, and in the low-frequency, infinite-relaxation-time limit, the longitudinal currents correlate with the topological properties of the magnon system.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for controlling magnon transport via light and reveals connections between photocurrents and magnon band topology in 2D ferromagnets.

title: Attosecond Molecular Physics In Large (bio) Molecules: A Perspective On An Unexplored Landscape
authors: V Despré, S Palakkal, E Munaro-Langloÿs And F Lépine
abstract: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized attosecond science and technology, which allows us to understand and control the properties of matter by accessing electron dynamics at the Angstrom length scale. Attosecond science and technology are currently being applied to investigate all phases of matter and have garnered particular attention in the field of light-induced processes in molecules. After two decades of development, an attosecond perspective on molecular processes has become a tangible reality thanks to advanced experiments and theories. However, so far, this has only been applied to small model systems. This article discusses the current state of the field and explores how it could expand to include the study of complex structures, including large biomolecules.
tldr: This perspective discusses the current state and future prospects of attosecond molecular physics, focusing on extending ultrafast electron-dynamics studies from small model systems to large biomolecules.
motivation: Attosecond science has enabled real-time observation of electron dynamics, but applications have so far been limited to small molecules, leaving complex biomolecular systems largely unexplored.
method: The article reviews existing attosecond experimental and theoretical approaches and outlines conceptual pathways for scaling them to large (bio)molecules.
result: It identifies challenges and opportunities for probing electron dynamics in complex molecular environments at the attosecond timescale.
conclusion: Expanding attosecond molecular physics to large biomolecules represents an unexplored landscape with potential for new insights into light-induced processes in biological matter.

title: Turbulent Magnetogenesis And Large-scale Magnetic Dynamo Amplification In Ion–electron Plasmas
authors: Fabio Bacchini, Francesco Pucci, Sergio Servidio, Francesco Valentini And William H Matthaeus
abstract: Using fully kinetic simulations that capture unprecedentedly large (from electron to ion) scales, we study magnetogenesis driven by continuous large-scale forcing until nonlinear dynamo saturation. We uncover a two-stage mechanism in collisionless ion–electron plasmas whose dynamics diverge dramatically from the pair-plasma case. In the first phase, electron pressure anisotropy triggers electron-Weibel modes, seeding small-scale magnetic fields. Then, a second growth phase emerges when the more massive ions develop their own strong anisotropy and drive ion-Weibel-type modes; concurrently, a Biermann-battery mechanism contributes to amplifying the magnetic field. This combined dynamics provides a tenfold amplification of the magnetic field in comparison to the pair-plasma case. Over long times, dynamo action continues until the system reaches a statistical steady state. This self-consistent kinetic mechanism provides a plausible explanation for robust magnetogenesis wherever an external forcing continuously stirs the plasma.
tldr: Fully kinetic simulations reveal a two-stage Weibel-type magnetogenesis mechanism in collisionless ion-electron plasmas, with electron then ion pressure anisotropy driving magnetic field amplification until dynamo saturation.
motivation: The origin of cosmic magnetic fields remains an open problem, and the role of kinetic instabilities in seeding and amplifying fields in ion-electron plasmas is not fully understood.
method: Large-scale particle-in-cell simulations spanning electron to ion scales with continuous large-scale forcing, comparing ion-electron and pair-plasma dynamics.
result: A tenfold magnetic field amplification compared to pair plasmas arises from electron-Weibel seeding followed by ion-Weibel growth and a Biermann-battery contribution, eventually reaching a statistical steady state.
conclusion: The self-consistent kinetic mechanism provides a plausible explanation for robust magnetogenesis in continuously stirred collisionless plasmas.

title: Altermagnetism And Superconductivity: A Short Historical Review
authors: Hui Hu And Xia-Ji Liu Zhao Liu
abstract: This review is organized into three parts. In the first part, we explore the deep interconnections among three seemingly unrelated concepts in condensed matter physics: electronic liquid crystal (ELC) phases, multipole expansions, and altermagnetism (AM). At the heart of these phenomena lies a shared foundation: spin-momentum locking in the nonrelativistic regime. Originally proposed in the context of ELC phases, nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking (NRSML) was later elegantly incorporated into the formalism of multipole expansions. This framework can be further extended across multiple atomic sites, making it particularly effective for describing AMs, which host localized magnetic moments with anisotropic magnetization densities distributed over sublattices. In the second part, we examine superconducting (SC) phenomena associated with AM from three complementary perspectives. First, we investigate SC associated with NRSML Fermi surfaces (FSs), the unifying theme of the first part, highlighting a rich variety of unconventional SC states. These include finite-momentum pairing, -wave and spin-triplet SC, and topological Bogoliubov FSs, among others. We then review SC emerging from either static AM order or AM fluctuations. Finally, we discuss the possible competition and intertwining between AM order and SC, illustrated using the repulsive Hubbard model. Additional related topics are addressed in the concluding part. Overall, this work offers both an accessible introduction to the newly identified magnetic order known as AM and a conceptual guide for researchers aiming to harness the ensuing unconventional SC in the development of future quantum technologies.
tldr: A review connecting electronic liquid crystal phases, multipole expansions, and altermagnetism via nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking, and surveying the unconventional superconductivity that can emerge from altermagnetic order or fluctuations.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a recently identified magnetic order hosting anisotropic magnetization densities on sublattices, and its interplay with superconductivity may enable novel unconventional pairing states relevant to future quantum technologies.
method: Conceptual and historical review that unifies electronic liquid crystal phases, multipole expansions, and nonrelativistic spin-momentum locking, then surveys superconductivity from NRSML Fermi surfaces, static altermagnetic order, altermagnetic fluctuations, and Hubbard-model studies.
result: The review catalogs a variety of superconducting states associated with altermagnetism, including finite-momentum pairing, d-wave and spin-triplet superconductivity, and topological Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, plus competition and intertwining effects in the repulsive Hubbard model.
conclusion: The paper serves as an accessible introduction to altermagnetism and a conceptual guide for exploiting the resulting unconventional superconductivity in future quantum technologies.

title: Superconductivity In Ruddlesden–Popper Nickelates: A Review Of Recent Progress, Focusing On Thin Films
authors: Yang Zhang, Fang-Ling Lin, Thomas A Maier And Elbio Dagotto
abstract: The discovery of superconductivity with K in the nickelate Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) bilayer La Ni O at high pressure has opened a new platform for unconventional superconductivity, followed by the subsequent observation of superconductivity in trilayer La Ni O , also at high pressure. Remarkably, ambient-pressure superconductivity was also observed recently in La Ni O ultra-thin films when grown on substrates that provide compressive strain. This discovery significantly extends the type of experimental techniques that can be used in nickelates, previously limited due to the high-pressure constraint. Discussing the similarities and differences among these nickel oxides will provide new insights into understanding the mechanism of high- superconductivity in correlated electron systems. In this paper, we review the experimental and theoretical progress on RP nickelates, with emphasis on thin films, and discuss future perspectives and research directions.
tldr: This review summarizes recent experimental and theoretical progress on superconductivity in Ruddlesden–Popper nickelates, with a focus on thin-film realizations under ambient pressure.
motivation: The discovery of superconductivity in nickelates at high pressure and later in strained thin films offers a new platform for unconventional superconductivity, motivating a comprehensive review of similarities and differences among these nickel oxides.
method: The authors review and synthesize experimental and theoretical literature on Ruddlesden–Popper nickelates, emphasizing thin-film growth, substrate-induced strain, and the resulting superconducting properties.
result: The review highlights key findings on high-pressure and ambient-pressure superconductivity in bilayer, trilayer, and thin-film nickelates, comparing their electronic and structural properties to understand the underlying mechanism.
conclusion: The paper concludes by outlining future research directions for nickelate superconductors, particularly thin-film-based studies that may reveal the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity in correlated electron systems.

title: Emergent Odd Viscoelasticity In Chiral Soft Glassy Materials
authors: Debarghya Banerjee And Peter Sollich
abstract: Rheological properties of chiral active materials have been an important area of research in the recent past, in particular regarding odd terms in their mechanical response. While much progress has been made in the study of odd viscous fluids and odd elastic solids, there is still a lack of understanding of odd viscoelastic responses. We introduce a chiral soft glassy rheology model to understand the emergence and nature of such odd viscoelastic responses in a class of amorphous solids. We use this model, which effectively considers an ensemble of actively rotating inclusions in a glassy matrix, to study the linear stress response to steady and oscillatory shear flows. For steady shear we find an odd viscosity that, non-trivially, grows as the active rotation frequency decreases. In oscillatory shear we find an odd viscoelastic spectrum with a non-trivial dependence on the driving frequency , combining resonance effects around with glassy power laws at larger .
tldr: The paper introduces a chiral soft glassy rheology model to study emergent odd viscoelastic responses in amorphous solids.
motivation: Chiral active materials have shown odd viscous and odd elastic responses, but odd viscoelastic behavior remains poorly understood.
method: An ensemble of actively rotating inclusions in a glassy matrix is modeled to compute linear stress responses under steady and oscillatory shear.
result: Steady shear yields an odd viscosity that grows as active rotation frequency decreases, while oscillatory shear produces an odd viscoelastic spectrum with resonance and glassy power-law regimes.
conclusion: The model provides a framework for understanding odd viscoelasticity in chiral soft glassy materials, revealing nontrivial frequency-dependent rheological signatures.

title: Advances In Laser-assisted Nuclear Decay And Nuclear Excitation
authors: Q Xiao, J H Cheng, Y Y Xu, Y T Zou, Z Z Ren, A Ya Dzyublik And T P Yu
abstract: From the synthesis and evolution of the elements to the celestial nuclear processes of stellar explosions and neutron star mergers, nuclear physics is the foundation of our understanding of the Universe. After more than a century of progress, the field of nuclear physics remains vibrant. The rapid advancement of laser technology has opened unprecedented avenues in nuclear physics, driven by the interdisciplinary convergence of laser physics, nuclear structure, plasma science, and quantum dynamics. This emerging field enables studies on laser-induced nuclear excitation, laser-assisted nuclear decay, and precision manipulation of nuclear isomers for optical clocks. This review comprehensively examines the research achievements over the past decade regarding the influence of lasers on radioactive charged-particle emissions and nuclear excitation. Regarding theoretical developments, the review details various methods used to evaluate the interactions between lasers and nuclei, including the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for decay, proton radioactivity, and two-proton radioactivity and Fermi’s golden rule for nuclear excitation as well as the application and advancement of various theoretical models and approximation methods. In experimental research, the review synthesizes significant breakthroughs in laser-induced nuclear excitation experiments, particularly emphasizing the excitation of the Th, Kr, and Sc. These achievements provide essential groundwork for future breakthroughs in both fundamental nuclear science and its broader technological applications.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental progress over the past decade on laser-assisted nuclear decay and laser-induced nuclear excitation.
motivation: Rapid advances in laser technology have opened new interdisciplinary avenues in nuclear physics, enabling studies of laser-induced nuclear excitation, laser-assisted decay, and precision manipulation of nuclear isomers for optical clocks.
method: The review surveys theoretical frameworks such as the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for decay, proton and two-proton radioactivity, and Fermi's golden rule for nuclear excitation, along with various models and approximation methods, and synthesizes experimental breakthroughs.
result: Significant experimental breakthroughs in laser-induced nuclear excitation are highlighted, particularly for Th, Kr, and Sc, alongside comprehensive coverage of theoretical methods for laser-nucleus interactions.
conclusion: These achievements provide essential groundwork for future breakthroughs in fundamental nuclear science and its broader technological applications, such as nuclear clocks and isomer manipulation.

title: Symmetry-enriched Topological Order In Tensor Networks: Defects, Gauging And Anyon Condensation
authors: Dominic J. Williamson, Nick Bultinck, And Frank Verstraete
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2199 (2026).

We study symmetry-enriched topological order in two-dimensional tensor network states by using graded matrix product operator algebras to represent symmetry-induced domain walls. A close connection to the theory of graded unitary fusion categories is established. Tensor network representations of the topological defect superselection sectors are constructed for all domain walls. The emergent symmetry-enriched topological order is extracted from these representations, including the symmetry action on the underlying anyons. Dual phase transitions, induced by gauging a global symmetry, and condensation of a bosonic subtheory, are analyzed and the relationship between topological orders on either side of the transition is derived. Several examples are worked through explicitly.

.

title: Promise Of Graph Sparsification And Decomposition For Noise Reduction In Qaoa: Analysis For Trapped-Ion Compilations
authors: Jai Moondra, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Greg Mohler, And Swati Gupta
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2185 (2026).

We develop new approximate compilation schemes that significantly reduce the expense of compiling the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for solving the Max-Cut problem. Our main focus is on compilation with trapped-ion simulators using Pauli-[MATH] operations and all-to-all Ising Hamiltonian [MATH] evolution generated by Molmer-Sorensen or optical dipole force interactions, though some of our results also apply to standard gate-based compilations. Our results are based on principles of graph sparsification and decomposition; the former reduces the number of edges in a graph while maintaining its cut structure, while the latter breaks a weighted graph into a small number of unweighted graphs. Though these techniques have been used as heuristics in various hybrid quantum algorithms, there have been no guarantees on their performance, to the best of our knowledge. This work provides the first provable guarantees using sparsification and decomposition to improve quantum noise resilience and reduce quantum circuit complexity.
